pointers.sentence: Called on a class it uses `decorate_class`, on any other callable `decorate_callable`, and refuses anything else with a `TypeError` (`django/test/utils.py:TestContextDecorator.__call__`).

`SimpleTestCase` runs a test method through `async_to_sync` only if it is a coroutine function, which the wrapper is ([One test, in order: `SimpleTestCase`](simple-test-case.md); `django/test/utils.py:TestContextDecorator.decorate_callable`, `django/test/testcases.py:SimpleTestCase._setup_and_call`).

`SimpleTestCase` runs a test method through `async_to_sync` only if it is a coroutine function, which the wrapper is ([One test, in order: `SimpleTestCase`](simple-test-case.md); `django/test/utils.py:TestContextDecorator.decorate_callable`, `django/test/testcases.py:SimpleTestCase._setup_and_call`).
It does not hold in `setUpClass`, and a subclass that defines a `setUp` without calling its parent's loses it (`django/test/utils.py:TestContextDecorator.decorate_class`).

On a class, `override_settings.decorate_class` replaces no `setUp`: it takes only a subclass of `SimpleTestCase`, refusing any other with a `ValueError`, "Only subclasses of Django SimpleTestCase can be decorated with override_settings", and records the values as `SimpleTestCase._overridden_settings` (`django/test/utils.py:override_settings.decorate_class`).

`SimpleTestCase.setUpClass` enters an `override_settings` of those values with `unittest.TestCase.enterClassContext`, which leaves it as a class cleanup, after `tearDownClass` (`django/test/testcases.py:SimpleTestCase.setUpClass`).

If a receiver raises while an override is entered, `override_settings.enable` keeps the exception as `override_settings.enable_exception` and calls `disable`, which restores the settings, sends the signal for leaving, and raises it (`django/test/utils.py:override_settings.enable`, `django/test/utils.py:override_settings.disable`).

Any other action, `"insert"` say, raises `ValueError` ("Unsupported action: insert") before the settings are touched (`django/test/utils.py:modify_settings.enable`).

`isolate_apps` gives a test its own app registry: `isolate_apps.enable` keeps `Options.default_apps`, puts in its place a new `Apps` populated with the applications it is given, and returns it (`django/test/utils.py:isolate_apps.enable`).

A new model's options take that registry as their `apps` unless its `Meta` gives one, and `ModelBase.__new__` registers a model that is not abstract there, not in the project's registry (`django/db/models/options.py:Options.__init__`, `django/db/models/options.py:Options.contribute_to_class`, `django/db/models/base.py:ModelBase.__new__`).

The documentation calls the arguments app labels, but `Apps` takes them as entries of `INSTALLED_APPS`: `isolate_apps("office")` raises `ModuleNotFoundError`, "No module named 'office'" (`docs/topics/testing/tools.txt`; `django/apps/registry.py:Apps.populate`).

`override_script_prefix` sets a script prefix and puts the old one back ([The script prefix, the current URLconf and the caches](../urls/state.md); `django/test/utils.py:override_script_prefix`).

`override_system_checks` leaves the check registry only the checks it is given, and the deployment checks too when its second argument is not `None` ([The system checks](../commands/checks.md); `django/test/utils.py:override_system_checks.enable`).
`ignore_warnings` adds an `"ignore"` filter inside `warnings.catch_warnings`, which leaving restores (`django/test/utils.py:ignore_warnings.enable`).
